patch.summary: Keap migration guide: inventory → rehearse → freeze → validate integrations — grounded in researched limitations and catalogue peers.

blocks.body: Migrate to Keap by inventorying legacy crm fields, mapping them to Keap objects, rehearsing a freeze window, and validating Gmail, Stripe, PayPal before reopening writes.
bullets: Inventory → map → rehearse → cut over → reopen
Highest risk: Base plans start at list price annually for two users; additional users are list price each.
Success signal: contact management works for the pilot cohort

blocks.heading: Keap migration cutover playbook
blocks.body: Migrations fail from optimistic timelines — not from missing motivation.

scenarios.title: Field inventory
scenarios.body: Export legacy fields that power contact management, lead management, pipeline management and mark must-map vs archive.

scenarios.title: Rehearsal load
scenarios.body: Run a non-prod load into Keap; measure match rates before the freeze.

scenarios.title: Production freeze
scenarios.body: Freeze legacy writes; cut over; validate Gmail; then reopen.

steps.label: Migrate when Small businesses needing CRM + marketing automation in one platform outweigh migration cost
Delay if this limitation hits cutover: Base plans start at list price annually for two users; additional users are list price each.
If Keap mapping is poor, compare destination fit with Capsule before moving data twice

items.title: No freeze window
items.body: Dual-writing without a freeze creates irrevocable duplicates.

items.title: Integrations last
items.body: Wire Gmail in rehearsal — not on Monday morning after cutover.

items.title: Data risk 1
items.body: Base plans start at list price annually for two users; additional users are list price each.

items.title: Data risk 2
items.body: Contact capacity and voice/SMS allotments scale by Max tier; overages apply for texts/voice minutes.

items.title: Data risk 3
items.body: Annual contracts may include a documented early-termination fee (list price) if cancelled before term end.
